question.text: The mole fraction of a solute in a solution is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>0</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>1</mn></math>. At <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>298</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">K</mi></math>, the molarity of this solution is the same as its molality. The density of this solution at <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>298</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">K</mi></math> is <math><mn>2.0</mn><mi mathvariant="normal"> </mi><mi mathvariant="normal">g</mi><mi mathvariant="normal"> </mi><mi mathvariant="normal">c</mi><msup><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></mrow><mrow><mo>–</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></msup></math>. The ratio of the molecular weights of the solute and solvent, <math><mfenced separators="|"><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">M</mi><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">W</mi></mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">o</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">l</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">u</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">t</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">e</mi></mrow></msub></mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">M</mi><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">W</mi></mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">o</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">l</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">v</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">e</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">n</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">t</mi></mrow></msub></mrow></mfrac></mrow></mfenced></math>, is:

solution.text:
1 mole solution has 0.1 mole solute and 0.9 mole solvent.
Let M1=Molar mass of solute
M2=Molar mass of solvent
Molality, m=0.10.9 M2×1000…..1
Molarity, M=0.10.1 M1+0.9 M2×2×1000…..2
∵m=M
⇒0.1×10000.9 M2=2000.1 M1+0.9 M2
⇒M1M2=9
